notes:
1. K. Kamarajar — Overview

  • Kumaraswami Kamaraj was one of the most influential political leaders of twentieth-century Tamil Nadu.
  • He was:
  • A freedom fighter.
  • Congress organiser.
  • Chief Minister of Madras State.
  • President of the Indian National Congress.
  • Major national political strategist.
  • He became especially famous for the expansion of:
  • School education.
  • Rural infrastructure.
  • Irrigation.
  • Industrial development.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → Education + Madras Chief Minister + Kamaraj Plan + Kingmaker

2. Popular Names

Kamarajar is popularly remembered as:

  • Karmaveerar Kamarajar.
  • Perunthalaivar Kamarajar.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Perunthalaivar → K. Kamarajar

3. Birth

  • Kamarajar was born on 15 July 1903.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → 15 July 1903

4. Birthplace

  • He was born at Virudupatti, present-day Virudhunagar in Tamil Nadu.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → Virudhunagar

5. Father

  • His father was Kumaraswami Nadar.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar's Father → Kumaraswami Nadar

6. Mother

  • His mother was Sivakami Ammal.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar's Mother → Sivakami Ammal

7. Family Background

  • Kamarajar belonged to a modest trading family.
  • His father was involved in business.

8. Father's Death

  • Kamarajar lost his father at a young age.
  • The family's financial position became difficult afterward.

9. School Education

  • Kamarajar's formal schooling ended early.
  • He entered employment while still young to support his family.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Kamarajar → Limited Formal Schooling → Major Expansion of Public Education Later

10. "Padikkatha Methai"

  • Kamarajar is popularly remembered by the Tamil expression "Padikkatha Methai," meaning an unusually wise person despite limited formal schooling.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

This is a popular honorific, not a claim that he lacked knowledge or political education.

11. Self-Education

  • Kamarajar developed political knowledge through:
  • Newspapers.
  • Public meetings.
  • Political discussions.
  • Congress activity.
  • Travel.

12. Early Political Atmosphere

His youth coincided with:

  • Home Rule agitation.
  • Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
  • Rise of Gandhi.
  • Non-Cooperation Movement.

13. Jallianwala Bagh Influence

  • The Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 1919 strongly affected nationalist opinion throughout India.
  • Kamarajar's political involvement deepened during this period.

14. Entry into Congress

  • Kamarajar joined the Indian National Congress as a young man around 1919.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → Joined Congress → Around 1919

15. Age at Political Entry

  • He was only in his mid-teens when he became deeply involved in Congress politics.

16. Virudhunagar Congress Work

  • Virudhunagar became the base of his earliest political work.
  • He attended meetings and organised Congress activity locally.

17. S. Satyamurti

  • S. Satyamurti became one of Kamarajar's most important political mentors.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar's Political Mentor → S. Satyamurti

18. Satyamurti's Importance

  • Satyamurti was:
  • A major Congress leader.
  • Parliamentarian.
  • Organiser from the Madras Presidency.

19. Kamarajar as Organiser

  • Kamarajar's greatest early political strength was organisation rather than public oratory.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Kamarajar → Grassroots Organisation

20. Congress Tours

  • He travelled extensively through villages and towns.
  • This gave him detailed knowledge of:
  • Local leaders.
  • Rural problems.
  • Congress workers.

21. Non-Cooperation Era

  • Kamarajar became active during the Gandhian mass-movement period that began with Non-Cooperation.

22. Khadi

  • Like other Congress workers, he supported:
  • Khadi.
  • Swadeshi.
  • Boycott of foreign goods.

23. Public Meetings

  • Kamarajar helped organise nationalist meetings despite police restrictions.

24. Flag and Nationalist Campaigns

  • During the 1920s he participated in Congress agitations connected with:
  • National flags.
  • Political mobilisation.
  • Civil rights.

25. Vaikom Context

  • Kamarajar's political rise occurred during the period when South Indian Congress leaders were involved in social-reform struggles such as Vaikom.
  • His principal historical significance, however, lay in Congress organisation and later governance.

26. Simon Commission

  • The Simon Commission arrived in India in 1928.
  • Congress organised nationwide opposition because the Commission contained no Indian member.

27. Kamarajar and Anti-Simon Politics

  • Kamarajar participated in the broader Congress mobilisation against British constitutional policies during this period.

28. Civil Disobedience Movement

  • Gandhi launched the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930.

29. Salt Satyagraha

  • Salt-law violation became the major symbol of Civil Disobedience.

30. Vedaranyam Salt March

  • C. Rajagopalachari led the Vedaranyam Salt Satyagraha in Tamil Nadu in 1930.
📌 Must-Memorise

Vedaranyam → Rajaji → 1930

31. Kamarajar and Civil Disobedience

  • Kamarajar participated in Civil Disobedience activities and was imprisoned by the British.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → Imprisoned During Civil Disobedience

32. Jail Experience

  • Imprisonment became an important part of Kamarajar's freedom-struggle career.
  • He spent several periods in British prisons.

33. Congress Organisation in the 1930s

  • During the 1930s Kamarajar steadily strengthened his position within the Tamil Nadu Congress organisation.

34. Grassroots Network

His network included:

  • Village-level workers.
  • District Congress committees.
  • Trade and community organisations.
  • Local nationalist leaders.

35. 1937 Provincial Elections

  • Elections were held under the Government of India Act 1935.
  • Congress performed strongly in the Madras Presidency.

36. Rajaji Ministry

  • C. Rajagopalachari became Premier of the Madras Presidency in 1937.

37. Kamarajar's Congress Role

  • Kamarajar concentrated heavily on party organisation rather than ministerial office during this phase.

38. Congress Ministries Resign

  • Congress provincial ministries resigned in 1939 after Britain involved India in World War II without consulting Indian leaders.
📌 Must-Memorise

Congress Ministries Resigned → 1939

39. Tamil Nadu Congress Committee

  • Kamarajar rose to become one of the most powerful leaders of the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee.

40. TNCC President

  • He served for many years as President of the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → Long-Time TNCC Organiser

41. Satyamurti–Kamarajar Partnership

  • Satyamurti's political guidance combined with Kamarajar's organisational ability helped strengthen Congress in Tamil Nadu.

42. Individual Satyagraha

  • Gandhi launched Individual Satyagraha in 1940.
  • Kamarajar became involved in wartime Congress opposition.

43. Wartime Arrests

  • British authorities arrested many Congress workers, including Kamarajar, during wartime nationalist campaigns.

44. Quit India Movement

  • Congress launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942.
📌 Must-Memorise

Quit India → 1942

45. Kamarajar and Quit India

  • Kamarajar actively worked to spread the Quit India message in Tamil Nadu.
  • He was subsequently arrested.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → Quit India Activities → Imprisonment

46. Underground Organising

  • Before his arrest, Kamarajar travelled to communicate Congress decisions and mobilise workers.

47. Freedom-Struggle Imprisonment

  • Kamarajar spent a cumulative period of several years in prison during British rule.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Kamarajar → Repeated Imprisonment as Freedom Fighter

48. Independence

  • India became independent on 15 August 1947.

49. Post-Independence Congress

  • After independence, Kamarajar became increasingly important in:
  • State politics.
  • Congress organisation.
  • National leadership.

50. Madras Presidency to Madras State

  • After the Constitution came into force in 1950, the former Madras Presidency functioned as Madras State.

51. Madras State — Linguistic Complexity

Madras State initially included substantial areas speaking:

  • Tamil.
  • Telugu.
  • Malayalam.
  • Kannada.

52. Andhra State

  • Andhra State was created in 1953 from Telugu-speaking areas of Madras State.
📌 Must-Memorise

Andhra State → 1953

53. Potti Sriramulu

  • Potti Sriramulu's death after a prolonged fast accelerated the demand for a Telugu-speaking state.

54. Political Transition

  • The reorganisation of Madras State created major political and administrative challenges.

55. Rajaji as Chief Minister

  • C. Rajagopalachari served as Chief Minister of Madras State from 1952 to 1954.

56. Kula Kalvi Controversy

  • Rajaji's Modified Scheme of Elementary Education became popularly criticised as the Kula Kalvi scheme.

57. Opposition

  • The scheme faced opposition from:
  • Periyar.
  • DMK.
  • Sections of Congress.
  • Other social groups.

58. Rajaji Resigns

  • Rajaji resigned as Chief Minister in 1954.

59. Kamarajar Becomes Chief Minister

  • K. Kamarajar became Chief Minister of Madras State on 13 April 1954.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → Madras Chief Minister → 13 April 1954

60. Chief Ministerial Tenure

  • Kamarajar served as Chief Minister from 1954 to 1963.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar CM → 1954–1963

61. Political Style

  • His administration became known for:
  • Simplicity.
  • Accessibility.
  • Focus on practical development.

62. Rural Tours

  • Kamarajar travelled extensively through rural areas while Chief Minister.
  • He often gathered information directly from local residents and officials.

63. Education — Central Priority

  • Expansion of school education became one of the defining achievements of his government.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar Government → School Expansion

64. School Accessibility

  • His government sought to place schools within easier reach of rural children.

65. New Schools

  • Large numbers of elementary and secondary schools were opened during his tenure.

66. Closed Schools Reopened

  • Schools that had earlier been closed in some areas were reopened as part of the drive to widen access.

67. Rural Education

  • Special attention was given to villages lacking convenient educational facilities.

68. Enrolment

  • School enrolment rose substantially during the Kamarajar period.

69. Free Education

  • The state expanded access to free schooling for children from poorer families.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Kamarajar → Wider Free Education

70. School Infrastructure

Expansion included:

  • Classrooms.
  • Teachers.
  • Rural schools.
  • Educational facilities.

71. Noon-Meal Programme

  • The school noon-meal programme was greatly expanded during Kamarajar's administration.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → Major Expansion of School Noon-Meal Programme

72. Important Historical Caution

  • School feeding schemes had existed earlier in parts of the Madras Presidency, including Madras Corporation initiatives.
  • Kamarajar's importance lies particularly in expanding the programme more broadly as part of the state's education drive.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Do Not Simplify as "Kamarajar Invented the First-Ever Noon Meal Scheme"

73. Purpose of Noon Meal

The programme sought to:

  • Increase enrolment.
  • Reduce dropout.
  • Encourage poor children to attend school.
  • Address hunger among pupils.

74. Education and Poverty

  • Kamarajar recognised that poor children could not attend school regularly if economic hardship forced them to work or remain hungry.

75. School Uniforms

  • Provision of school uniforms to disadvantaged children became another measure associated with expanding educational participation.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar Era → School Uniform Support

76. Social Inclusion

Education policy attempted to improve access for:

  • Rural children.
  • Poor families.
  • Socially disadvantaged communities.

77. "Kalvi Thanthai"

  • Kamarajar is popularly honoured in Tamil Nadu for his contribution to education.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Kamarajar → Education-Oriented Chief Minister

78. Education as Development

  • He regarded basic schooling as essential to:
  • Individual opportunity.
  • Economic development.
  • Social mobility.

79. Teacher Expansion

  • The rapid increase in schools required recruitment and deployment of more teachers.

80. Kamarajar vs Kula Kalvi

Rajaji period:

  • Modified Elementary Education Scheme controversy.

Kamarajar period:

  • Greater emphasis on regular school expansion and wider access.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite Comparison

Rajaji → Kula Kalvi Controversy

Kamarajar → School Expansion

81. Irrigation — Major Priority

  • Kamarajar's government invested heavily in irrigation projects.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → Education + Irrigation + Industry

82. Agriculture

  • Irrigation development aimed to:
  • Expand cultivated area.
  • Stabilise agriculture.
  • Improve rural incomes.

83. Lower Bhavani Project

  • The Lower Bhavani Project became one of the important irrigation schemes associated with post-independence Tamil Nadu development.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Lower Bhavani → Major Irrigation Project

84. Manimuthar Dam

  • Manimuthar Dam was developed during the Kamarajar era.
📌 Must-Memorise

Manimuthar → Kamarajar-Era Irrigation

85. Vaigai Dam

  • Vaigai Dam was another major project completed during his tenure.
📌 Must-Memorise

Vaigai Dam → Kamarajar Era

86. Sathanur Dam

  • Sathanur Dam across the Thenpennai system became an important irrigation project.
📌 Must-Memorise

Sathanur Dam → Kamarajar Era

87. Krishnagiri Reservoir

  • Irrigation projects were also developed in northern Tamil areas, including the Krishnagiri region.

88. Amaravathi Dam

  • Amaravathi Dam was another significant project associated with this development phase.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Kamarajar Period → Multiple Dam and Irrigation Projects

89. Irrigation Impact

The projects supported:

  • Agriculture.
  • Drinking water.
  • Rural development.
  • Electricity in some multipurpose contexts.

90. Electrification

  • Rural electrification expanded during Kamarajar's tenure.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → Rural Electrification

91. Electricity and Agriculture

  • Electricity supported:
  • Irrigation pumps.
  • Rural industries.
  • Household development.

92. Industrial Development

  • Madras State experienced considerable industrial expansion during Kamarajar's administration.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar Era → Industrial Growth

93. Public-Sector Industry

  • His government supported establishment and expansion of major industrial projects with Union government cooperation.

94. Neyveli Lignite Corporation

  • Development of Neyveli lignite resources became a major industrial milestone in Tamil Nadu.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Neyveli → Lignite + Industrial Development

95. Neyveli Lignite Corporation

  • Neyveli Lignite Corporation was established in the 1950s.
  • The project became important for:
  • Mining.
  • Power generation.
  • Industrial growth.

96. Integral Coach Factory

  • The Integral Coach Factory at Perambur, Chennai, began production during the 1950s.
📌 Must-Memorise

Integral Coach Factory → Perambur

97. ICF Importance

  • It became one of India's major railway-coach manufacturing centres.

98. BHEL Tiruchirappalli Context

  • Heavy electrical and engineering industrial development around Tiruchirappalli expanded during the broader Kamarajar-era industrialisation phase.

99. Guindy Industrial Estate

  • Guindy Industrial Estate became an important centre for small and medium industry.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Guindy → Industrial Estate

100. Small Industries

  • Kamarajar's government encouraged:
  • Small industries.
  • Industrial estates.
  • Employment generation.

101. Sugar Industry

  • Expansion of irrigation and agriculture supported agro-based industries such as sugar production.

102. Paper and Cement

  • Tamil Nadu's industrial base expanded in sectors including:
  • Cement.
  • Paper.
  • Engineering.

103. Transport

  • Road development received increased attention under Kamarajar.

104. Rural Roads

  • Better roads connected:
  • Villages.
  • Markets.
  • Schools.
  • Administrative centres.

105. Public Works

Kamarajar's development model concentrated on practical infrastructure:

  • Schools.
  • Dams.
  • Roads.
  • Electricity.
  • Industries.

106. Administrative Reputation

  • Kamarajar developed a reputation for:
  • Personal simplicity.
  • Direct supervision.
  • Limited ostentation.

107. Cabinet Selection

  • He was known for selecting ministers and administrators based heavily on political utility and competence rather than personal luxury or status.

108. Political Inclusiveness

  • Kamarajar attempted to manage different factions within the Tamil Nadu Congress.

109. Electoral Success

  • Congress remained the dominant party in Madras State during most of his chief ministership.

110. 1957 Election

  • Congress retained power in Madras State after the 1957 Assembly election.

111. 1962 Election

  • Kamarajar again led Congress to victory in the 1962 state election.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → Congress Victories → 1957 + 1962

112. Rise of DMK

  • During Kamarajar's tenure, the DMK steadily expanded as a major opposition force.

113. Dravidian Politics

  • Tamil Nadu politics increasingly featured competition between:
  • Congress.
  • DMK.
  • Other regional and ideological groups.

114. Kamarajar's Response

  • Kamarajar relied heavily on:
  • Development.
  • Congress organisation.
  • Rural political networks.

115. Relationship with Periyar

  • Periyar and Kamarajar belonged to different political traditions.
  • Periyar at times expressed support for aspects of Kamarajar's educational and social-development record despite wider ideological differences.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Periyar and Kamarajar → Not Members of Same Political Movement

116. Relationship with Rajaji

  • Rajaji and Kamarajar were both major Congress leaders from Tamil Nadu.
  • They later differed politically.

117. Rajaji's Swatantra Party

  • Rajaji founded the Swatantra Party in 1959.
  • It became an opposition force against Congress policies.

118. Kamarajar and Nehru

  • Kamarajar maintained a strong political relationship with Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → Major Congress Leader During Nehru Era

119. National Congress Role

  • By the early 1960s, Kamarajar's influence extended far beyond Madras State.

120. Kamaraj Plan

  • In 1963, Kamarajar proposed the famous Kamaraj Plan.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamaraj Plan → 1963

121. Purpose of Kamaraj Plan

The plan proposed that:

  • Senior Congress ministers should leave government office.
  • They should devote themselves to strengthening the party organisation.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamaraj Plan → Ministers Leave Office → Strengthen Congress

122. Reason

  • Kamarajar believed prolonged occupation of office had weakened:
  • Party organisation.
  • Grassroots contact.
  • Public connection.

123. Kamarajar's Own Example

  • Kamarajar voluntarily resigned as Chief Minister under the spirit of his plan.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar Resigned CM → 1963 → Party Work

124. Date of Resignation

  • He left the Chief Minister's office in October 1963.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar CM Ends → 1963

125. Successor

  • M. Bhaktavatsalam succeeded Kamarajar as Chief Minister of Madras State.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → M. Bhaktavatsalam

126. Union Ministers

  • Several senior Union ministers also left office under the Kamaraj Plan.

127. National Impact

  • The Kamaraj Plan greatly increased Kamarajar's influence within the Congress organisation.

128. Congress President

  • Kamarajar became President of the Indian National Congress in 1964.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → INC President → 1964

129. Organisational Leadership

  • As Congress president, he became one of the most powerful decision-makers in national politics.

130. Nehru's Death

  • Jawaharlal Nehru died on 27 May 1964.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru → Died 1964

131. Prime-Ministerial Succession

  • Congress needed to select a new Prime Minister after Nehru's death.

132. Kamarajar's Role

  • Kamarajar consulted party leaders and helped build consensus around Lal Bahadur Shastri.
📌 Must-Memorise

After Nehru → Kamarajar Helped Select Lal Bahadur Shastri

133. Lal Bahadur Shastri

  • Shastri became Prime Minister in 1964.

134. "Kingmaker"

  • Kamarajar's central role in selecting national leadership earned him the popular description "Kingmaker."
📌 Must-Memorise

Kingmaker → K. Kamarajar

135. Shastri's Death

  • Lal Bahadur Shastri died at Tashkent on 11 January 1966.
📌 Must-Memorise

Shastri → Tashkent → 1966

136. Second Succession Crisis

  • Congress again had to choose a Prime Minister.

137. Indira Gandhi

  • Kamarajar played an important role in securing support for Indira Gandhi in the 1966 Congress leadership contest.
📌 Must-Memorise

1966 → Kamarajar Helped Indira Gandhi Become PM

138. Morarji Desai

  • Morarji Desai was Indira Gandhi's principal rival in the leadership contest.

139. Why "Kingmaker"

Kamarajar was associated with the selection of:

  • Lal Bahadur Shastri in 1964.
  • Indira Gandhi in 1966.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kingmaker → Shastri + Indira

140. Congress President Tenure

  • Kamarajar remained Congress president during a crucial period in the mid-1960s.

141. 1967 Elections

  • The 1967 elections marked a major turning point in Indian and Tamil Nadu politics.

142. Congress Defeat in Madras State

  • Congress lost power in Madras State in 1967.
  • DMK formed the government under C.N. Annadurai.
📌 Must-Memorise

1967 → DMK Defeated Congress → Annadurai CM

143. Kamarajar's Defeat

  • Kamarajar himself was defeated in the Virudhunagar Assembly constituency in 1967.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar Defeated → Virudhunagar → 1967

144. Significance

  • The defeat symbolised the decline of Congress dominance in Tamil Nadu and rise of Dravidian parties.

145. C.N. Annadurai

  • C.N. Annadurai became Chief Minister after the DMK victory.

146. Electoral Return

  • Kamarajar later returned to Parliament through the Nagercoil Lok Sabha constituency.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → Nagercoil Lok Sabha

147. Nagercoil By-Election

  • He won the Nagercoil parliamentary by-election in 1969.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nagercoil → Kamarajar → 1969

148. Congress Split

  • The Indian National Congress split in 1969.
📌 Must-Memorise

Congress Split → 1969

149. Congress (O)

  • Kamarajar became one of the principal leaders of Congress (Organisation), commonly called Congress (O).
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → Congress (O)

150. Indira Gandhi Faction

  • Prime Minister Indira Gandhi led the rival faction that emerged from the split.

151. "Syndicate"

  • Kamarajar was associated with the group of senior Congress organisational leaders often described as the Syndicate.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Kamarajar → Congress Organisation / Syndicate

152. Syndicate — Caution

  • "Syndicate" was an informal political label.
  • It was not the formal name of a constitutional institution.

153. Presidential Election 1969

  • The presidential election of 1969 intensified the Congress split.

154. Neelam Sanjiva Reddy

  • The official Congress organisational leadership supported Neelam Sanjiva Reddy.

155. V.V. Giri

  • V.V. Giri contested independently and ultimately won with support from Indira Gandhi's political strategy.

156. Congress Division

  • The conflict resulted in a formal organisational split between Indira Gandhi and the older Congress leadership.

157. Kamarajar After Split

  • Kamarajar continued to lead the organisational Congress tradition.

158. 1971 Election

  • Congress (O) faced major electoral difficulties against Indira Gandhi's Congress in the 1971 general election.

159. Kamarajar's Popular Standing

  • Despite national organisational decline, Kamarajar retained substantial personal respect in Tamil Nadu.

160. Personal Simplicity

  • He was widely known for:
  • Simple dress.
  • Modest personal lifestyle.
  • Lack of ostentation.

161. Unmarried Life

  • Kamarajar never married.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamarajar → Unmarried

162. Personal Wealth

  • His public image emphasised limited personal wealth and a life centred on politics and public service.

163. Decision-Making Style

  • He was known for:
  • Listening.
  • Practical judgement.
  • Direct questioning.
  • Quick administrative decisions.

164. Limited Formal Education — Administrative Skill

  • His career became a famous example of practical political intelligence developing outside advanced formal education.

165. Development Model

Kamarajar's approach can be remembered as:

Education

  • Irrigation
  • Electricity
  • Industry
  • Roads

166. Education as Main Legacy

  • Among all his policies, expansion of school education became his strongest popular legacy in Tamil Nadu.

167. Rural School Strategy

  • Bringing schools closer to villages reduced the distance children had to travel.

168. Dropout Reduction

Measures such as:

  • Noon meals.
  • Uniforms.
  • School expansion.

helped address barriers to attendance.

169. Social Mobility

  • Wider schooling contributed to the long-term expansion of literacy and social mobility in Tamil Nadu.

170. Midday Meal — Later Development

  • Tamil Nadu's nutrition programmes were expanded and transformed further by later governments.
  • Kamarajar's period remains important for linking school feeding with mass educational expansion.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Kamarajar Scheme ≠ Entire Later Nutritious Meal Programme History

171. M.G. Ramachandran Connection

  • The later Nutritious Meal Programme associated with M.G. Ramachandran represented a subsequent major expansion of school feeding.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Kamarajar → Earlier Expansion of School Noon Meals

M.G.R. → Later Large-Scale Nutritious Meal Expansion

172. Tamil Nadu's Educational Tradition

  • Kamarajar's policies became an important foundation for Tamil Nadu's later reputation for widespread school access.

173. Industrial Legacy

Important industrial-development associations include:

  • Neyveli.
  • Perambur ICF.
  • Industrial estates.
  • Power expansion.

174. Irrigation Legacy

Important projects associated with the era include:

  • Vaigai.
  • Manimuthar.
  • Sathanur.
  • Amaravathi.
  • Lower Bhavani and related irrigation development.

175. Kamarajar and Agriculture

  • His government understood that industrialisation alone could not address the needs of a predominantly rural population.

176. Balanced Development

  • Education, agriculture and industry were pursued together.

177. Kamarajar and Centre–State Relations

  • His close relationship with national Congress leadership helped Madras State obtain support for major infrastructure and industrial projects.

178. Nehru–Kamarajar Relationship

Nehru:

  • National Prime Minister.

Kamarajar:

  • Major state leader and later national Congress organiser.

Their partnership connected:

  • Union planning.
  • Tamil Nadu development.

179. Kamarajar and Satyamurti

Satyamurti:

  • Mentor.

Kamarajar:

  • Organiser who later rose to state and national leadership.
📌 Must-Memorise

Satyamurti → Mentor of Kamarajar

180. Kamarajar and Rajaji

Rajaji:

  • Senior Gandhian.
  • Madras CM before Kamarajar.
  • Later Swatantra leader.

Kamarajar:

  • Congress organiser.
  • Expanded education.
  • Succeeded Rajaji in 1954.

181. Kamarajar and Annadurai

  • Annadurai led the DMK that ended Congress rule in Madras State in 1967.
  • Their rivalry represented the transition from Congress dominance to Dravidian-party government.

182. Kamarajar and Periyar

  • Periyar was an ideological social revolutionary outside Congress.
  • Kamarajar remained a Congress nationalist.
  • Their political paths were different despite occasional convergence on specific social questions.

183. Kamarajar and Indira Gandhi

  • Kamarajar helped Indira Gandhi become Prime Minister in 1966.
